role: kick (inside mic): LF thump + beater body; tighten sub, cut 250-500 box, modest 4 kHz click, no harsh top

measured.read: Mono kick-in, lots of clean headroom (-2.77 peak, crest 21). Energy centered at 58-63 Hz with a hot 31.5 Hz sub-rumble shelf; thump lump at 125 Hz; box descends 250-500 (315-400 worst); beater click peaks ~4 kHz; top rolls off hard above 6 kHz (no harsh top, hiss lives up there). polarity_inverted=true is the phase-align result, NOT a defect - leave it.

rationale: Mono kick-in mic with lots of clean headroom and a textbook kick-close profile: fundamental at 58-63 Hz, a hot 31.5 Hz sub-rumble shelf, a 125 Hz thump lump, box descending through 250-500 (315-400 worst), and the beater click peaking ~4 kHz before a hard rolloff above 6 kHz. Plan follows the brief and the kit's hiss caveat. CLEAN: gentle 30 Hz HPF (12 dB/oct) to shed sub-30 rumble without touching the 58 Hz fundamental; declick forced off (percussive); denoise off - the hiss lives above 6 kHz and we add no air, so no need to risk smearing transients. EQ (zero-phase): -3 dB bell at 31.5 Hz Q1.2 to tighten the sub shelf the meter flagged (cut, don't roll the whole bottom); -3.5 dB bell at 350 Hz Q1.1 - the box/mud center between the 315/400 troughs (this is the 250-500 cut the brief asks for, placed where the spectrum says box actually sits); a small -1.5 dB at 125 Hz Q1.4 to trim the secondary thump lump so it doesn't double the fundamental; one modest +2 dB at 4 kHz Q1.0 for beater click (4 kHz is the measured click peak, well below the harsh 5-7 kHz zone and below the hiss region - safe). No high-shelf, no excite, no de-harsh (nothing rings up top here), no dynamic EQ (box is constant, not level-dependent), no transient stage (punch comes from the API comp per the brief). API COLOR: HPF 40 Hz as a console-side safety below the HPF'd EQ. Comp ON, New (FF), 3:1, Medium attack (measured punchiest) with a moderate -4 thresh and 0.18 s release to grab body and add slam without choking the attack - punch from the 225, not EQ. 550 EQ kept conservative and the TOP FLAT: tiny +1 LF at 60 Hz for weight, -2 LMF at 350 reinforcing the box cut, +1 HMF at 4 kHz for a touch more click, and HF at 5 kHz held at 0 so 5 kHz is never stacked across hmf+hf (no harshness). Output peaked to -2 dBFS for safe downstream gain. Polarity inversion left intact - it is the phase-align result, not a defect.

role: kick beater / click mic — owns attack & beater click; the "in" mic owns thump. HPF the lows, bring out click/transient, tame brittle 5-7 kHz.

measured.third_octave_notes: 63Hz=0dB ref (LF-dominant), 50/80Hz hot, box at 315-400Hz (-12 to -13), click hump 2.5kHz(-17), brittle hump 5-6.3kHz(-15.2/-15.0), 16k/20k roll off to -31/-42
measured.read: Very transient mono beater mic (crest 20.6). LF-dominant (it's hearing the 'in' mic's thump it shouldn't own) plus a 315-400Hz cardboard box and a brittle 5-6.3kHz hump that overlaps the kit's known 5-7k harshness. No clipping/DC; preamp hiss present (no air/excite). Job: HPF the thump away, lift the 2.5-3.5kHz click, tame the brittle top, sharpen the attack — let the 225 comp do the punch.

rationale: Mono beater/click mic, crest 20.6, LF-dominant with dominant peak at 70 Hz that belongs to the "in" mic — so clean HPF=90 Hz hands the thump back to "in", with a matching EQ high_pass at 90 Hz. Preamp hiss is present so denoise=6 dB (gentle, before any top work) and NO excite/air shelf (would lift the hiss floor); 16k/20k already roll off naturally. Corrective EQ is cuts-first: -2.5 @ 200 and -3.5 @ 340 kill the boxy/cardboard zone the third-octave shows at 315-400 Hz, a modest +2.5 @ 3 kHz brings out the beater click (centroid 3300, click hump sits 2.5-4k, BELOW the harsh zone), and -2.5 @ 6 kHz trims the brittle 5-6.3 kHz hump that overlaps the kit's known 5-7k harshness. de_harsh is a gentle level-triggered suppressor over 5-7 kHz (depth 0.4, max 4 dB) so the click stays but the brittle ring only ducks when it spikes — safer than a bigger static cut. shape_bands sharpens the attack where it matters: transient +0.5/+1 dB in the 2-8 kHz click band, +0.1/-1 dB in the lows (de-emphasize the thump tail), neutral elsewhere. dynamic_eq null (the box is static, not level-dependent). API color: HPF 80 on the strip, Medium-attack New-FF 225 comp (measured punchiest) at 4:1 / thresh -6 / 0.12 s for the punch instead of EQ; 550 TOP KEPT FLAT — hmf only +1 @ 3 kHz, hf 0 @ 5 kHz (5 kHz lives in both bands, never stacked), and a small lmf -2 @ 350 to reinforce the de-box. Output peak target -3 dBFS leaves headroom.

role: snare top — crack + body close mic (mono, 48k, polarity-inverted, quiet at -30.5 LUFS, very peaky crest 28.8 dB)

measured.read: Body fundamental dominates at ~200 Hz (160-250 lump = the boxy tail); 1-5 kHz is flat with a small 3.1-5 kHz harsh nub; HF rolls off after 6.3k then 12.5-16k creeps back up = preamp hiss. Snap exists but isn't loud — add it via transient, not a hiss-raising HF boost.

rationale: Snare top is quiet (-30.5 LUFS) and very peaky (crest 28.8) with a body-dominant spectrum (peak ~200 Hz) and a hiss-carrying 12.5-16k creep. Plan: (1) clean — HPF 70 Hz removes sub rumble/bleed below the snare body; gentle 4 dB denoise BEFORE any brightening to keep the preamp hiss down (no excite, no HF shelf boost — both would lift the hiss floor). declick OFF (forced). (2) Static EQ — small 300 Hz bell cut (-2.5, Q1.1) tames the boxy 160-250 lump tail; small 5 kHz bell cut (-2.0, Q1.6) de-spits the harsh nub. Cuts only, modest. (3) de_harsh — Soothe-style dynamic suppressor over 3.5-6.5 kHz (depth 0.45, max -4 dB) ducks the 1-5 kHz harsh ring ONLY when it rings, leaving the crack intact between hits. (4) transient — add snap in the crack/attack bands (mid +0.25, presence +0.4) and lightly tighten the 8k+ band sustain (-1 dB gain, low hiss tail) — snap comes from transient shaping, not a hiss-raising boost. dynamic_eq null (box is static, the static cut handles it). (5) API color — KEEP THE 550 TOP FLAT: hmf/hf gain 0 (5 kHz lives in both bands; stacking = harsh). Punch comes from the 225 comp (New FF, Medium attack ≈ punchiest, ratio 3, thresh -10). Only a -2 dB LMF box cut at 300 and flat LF — conservative, role-appropriate console tone. Polarity is inverted (flagged) but the kit was already phase-aligned, so leave it.

role: snare bottom (wires mic) — buzz/snap character; HPF the LF junk, present 6–9 kHz wire buzz while guarding 5 kHz harshness

measured.read: Very dynamic mono bottom-snare mic (crest 27.6, peak -5.3, no clip). Energy lump 160-400 Hz peaking at 200 Hz is shell ring/box (junk on a wires mic), scooped mids 500-1k, then a 4-6.3 kHz wire-buzz plateau (5 kHz is the harshness edge). Top rolls off above 8k so no air is needed — and excite would only lift the preamp hiss.

rationale: Bottom-snare wires mic: all the useful character is the 6-9 kHz buzz/snap, not the low end. (1) clean: HPF 150 Hz to kill the shell-ring/box LF junk (dompeak 199 Hz is box, not body on a bottom mic), gentle 4 dB denoise AFTER the HPF to keep the known preamp hiss in check before any presence move; declick stays OFF (percussive). (2) apply-eq (phase=zero, keeps the phase-align intact): redundant safety HPF at 150, a -4.5 dB bell at 200 Hz on the box peak and a -2.5 dB bell at 400 Hz on the secondary box (cut the problem, don't boost around it), plus a modest +2.5 dB bell at 7 kHz — deliberately ABOVE the 5 kHz harsh edge — to present the wire buzz. (3) suppress-resonances 4.8-6.8 kHz, depth 0.45 / 4 dB max, to dynamically tame the harsh edge of that same wire plateau only when it rings, so the 7 kHz lift doesn't read brittle. No dynamic-eq (the box is constant, not level-dependent), no transient design (crest is already 27.6 dB — huge snap), no excite (top rolls off above 8k and excite would lift the hiss). (4) API color: HP 80 stacks under the clean HPF; New(FF) 225 comp at 3:1, Medium attack (measured punchiest) for wire snap, ~0.18 s release; 550 EQ does only small complementary cuts (LF -1.5, LMF -2) and a tiny HMF +1.5 — TOP KEPT FLAT (HF 0) so 5 kHz is never stacked across hmf/hf.

role: hi-hat (close mic) — salt-shaker hat, mono, 48 kHz

measured.read: Close hat with a fat 160-400 Hz whoosh/spill bulge (200 Hz is the single loudest band, 0.0 dB ref) and LF rumble at 63-80 Hz that has no business in a close hat; a 5 kHz harsh poke sits above its 4k/6.3k neighbors (brittleness zone); air rolls off above 8 kHz. Flat tilt = already bright/whooshy, not dull. +0.62 dBTP and 22 clipped samples are minor inter-sample overs cleaned by the HPF + headroom from cuts.

rationale: Measure-grounded close-hat cleanup. (1) clean: HPF 110 Hz kills the 63-80 Hz rumble/spill (no hat fundamental lives there) and trims the inter-sample overs; gentle 6 dB denoise tackles the known preamp hiss BEFORE any top lift so the air shelf doesn't amplify it. (2) apply-eq (zero-phase, attacks intact): the 200 Hz bell -4.5 dB is the headline move — 200 Hz is the single loudest band (0.0 ref) and is pure whoosh/spill; 400 Hz -3 dB clears the box; HPF mirrored in the EQ stage; one modest 11 kHz high-shelf +2 dB for air, kept small precisely because the floor is hissy. CUT the problem (whoosh/box), don't boost around it; air boost stays conservative. (3) de-harsh focused 5-7 kHz, depth 0.45 / max -4 dB — dynamic so it only ducks the 5 kHz poke when it rings, preserving the salt-shaker sizzle while killing the brittle edge the brief warns about. No static cut there because the harshness is transient, not constant. (4) No dynamic-eq: the 200 Hz whoosh is constant, so static EQ is the right tool. No transient design: this is a wash/sizzle source, not a punch stem. No excite: the floor is hissy and air excitement would raise it — the modest shelf is enough. (5) API color: 225 comp ON, New (FF), Medium attack (measured punchiest, and FF medium adds gentle density without grabbing the hat tail), ratio 3, thresh -8, release 0.1 s — punch from the comp not the EQ. 550 TOP KEPT FLAT: lmf -2 dB at 200 Hz reinforces the whoosh cut, hmf only +1 dB at 10k, hf 0 at 12k so 5 kHz is never stacked across hmf+hf (avoids re-introducing the harshness we just dynamically tamed). Output -1 dBFS for headroom into the next stage.

role: overheads (stereo) — cymbals + whole-kit image; carries the hi-hat

measured.read: Bright OH (centroid 2601, healthy 18.5 dB crest) but it carries a fat kick/tom mud + box lump: 63-80 Hz hump and a low-mid plateau peaking at 200 Hz (loudest band, 0.0 dB) thru 400 Hz. Harshness sits 3.15-6.3 kHz (3150/4000 proud against the slope). Air rolls off hard above 8 kHz; preamp hiss means no aggressive top boosts. True peak already +0.18 dBTP so the top is hot.

rationale: OH carries kick/tom mud + box, harsh 3-6k, thin top with audible preamp hiss. Order: clean first (HPF 140 to dump the 63-80 Hz kick lump and below the kit's dedicated kick mic; light denoise -4 dB to tame hiss BEFORE any air). Static EQ: -3.5 dB bell at 200 Hz (the single loudest band, the box) + a gentle -1.5 at 400 Hz, both modest cuts not gouges; a small +1.5 high-shelf at 12k for air that the gentle denoise keeps from amplifying hiss too far. De-harsh (suppress_resonances) focused 3.15-6.3k, depth 0.5 / max 4 dB — dynamic, ducks the cymbal/hat harshness only when it rings rather than dulling the whole top. No dynamic_eq (the mud is constant, static handles it). No transient shaping (18.5 dB crest is already healthy; punch comes from the API 225 comp). No excite — top is thin AND hissy, exciting air would raise the noise floor. API color stays conservative: console HPF 100 (under the corrective 140), 225 comp New(FF)/Medium-attack/2.5:1 for punch per the shootout, 550 TOP KEPT FLAT (hmf 5k = 0, hf 12.5k = +1 only) so 5 kHz is never stacked across hmf+hf; small lf/lmf trims (-2/-2) reinforce the de-mud. Output ceiling -1 dBFS since true peak is already hot at +0.18 dBTP."

role: room/ambience (stereo) — the kit "vibe" mic; very dynamic (crest 34.6), boxy low-mid hump, audible preamp hiss in the 6–13 kHz plateau, polarity already flipped by phase-align.

measured.read: Natural, very dynamic room with a clear boxy 200–400 Hz hump (peak 210 Hz) and a noisy preamp-hiss plateau that lifts 6.3–8 kHz above the 4–5 kHz region; lows are decorrelated (low-band width −14 dB) so HPF the sub before anything. Polarity already inverted by phase-align — do NOT re-flip.

rationale: Room/ambience mic: HPF 50 Hz first to drop the decorrelated sub-rumble (low-band width −14 dB, worst mono-sum loss in the lows) before any processing, plus a gentle 5 dB denoise for the audible preamp hiss — done BEFORE any top-end work since air/excite would raise that hiss (excite=null for the same reason). Corrective EQ targets the real boxy hump: −3.5 dB bell at 210 Hz (the dominant peak / third-octave mountain) and −2 dB at 400 Hz to open the low-mids, plus the HPF mirrored. de-harsh is a conservative dynamic suppressor over 2.5–6 kHz (depth 0.4, ≤4 dB) to tame ring/harshness only when it pokes above the envelope — no static high cut, so the room stays alive. No transient design (room wants its natural 34.6 dB crest, not snap) and no dynamic EQ (the boxiness is constant, a static cut handles it). For the API color: feedback (Old) comp at a soft 2:1, Medium attack for the punchiest behavior per the kit measurement, ~0.3 s release for glue/character (the role note flags this as a good comp/character candidate) without crushing the dynamics; the 550 top is kept FLAT (hmf/hf gain 0 — 5 kHz lives in both bands, never stack), with only small LF/LMF trims at 200/315 reinforcing the box cut. Polarity is left inverted — it was set by phase-align; flipping would break alignment with the overheads.
